propositions: When an ordered pair holds two differently-related net-active links (e.g. blocks and relates_to simultaneously via idempotent add_dependency per relation), pair-scoped removal via rebar.unlink(id1, id2) cannot express which relation to remove.

Guard G5 in apply_inbound_records.py declines inbound removal records when the peer-deleted relation does not match the pair's most-recent net-active relation, causing permanent non-convergence: the record re-emits and re-declines every pass.

Outbound link deduplication is direction-agnostic on vendor_type but not on relation, while inbound differs in per-relation local vocabulary, allowing inbound remove records to survive G4 suppression and reach G5 when vendor types collide across directions.

Removal must become relation-scoped, symmetric with write: graph/_links.remove_dependency keyed on (target_id, relation), with optional relation parameter threaded through the CLI and library facades while keeping pair-scoped behavior as default for backward compatibility.

A reconciler pass applying a double-related pair's peer-deleted link must converge by removing exactly the mirrored relation without removing any link the peer still carries, validated as a logged no-op when the named relation has no net-active local match.
